$comment: Registry of every `allow-raw` exemption in the codebase. An inline `// allow-raw: <id>` comment is only accepted by scripts/lint-raw-values.ts if a matching entry exists here for the same file. Run `npm run tokens:lint-values` after any change.

exemptions.reason: h-[calc(100%-1px)] — the active tab must overlap the 1px bottom border of the tab list. A subpixel offset derived from a border width has no equivalent in the spacing scale.
#ccc and #fff are values matched inside CSS attribute selectors ([stroke='#ccc']) against SVG attributes injected by Recharts at runtime. A custom property cannot appear inside an attribute selector.
z-1 raises the indicator above the menu bar border inside a local stacking context. The z-index scale addresses global layers (dropdown, modal, tooltip), not local ordering.
top-[60%] positions the arrow diamond relative to the indicator bar. A geometric ratio, not a spacing decision.
max-h-[80vh] caps the drawer height relative to the viewport. Viewport units are outside the spacing scale by design.
The translate-y calc compensates for the rotation of the arrow square so its tip lands exactly on the edge. Derived from the geometry, not from the spacing scale.
translate-x calc(100%-2px) compensates for the border inset of the thumb so it stops flush with the track edge.
z-0 creates a local stacking context so the range-highlight pseudo-elements paint below the day cells. Two occurrences, same rationale.
Canvas and CanvasText are CSS system color keywords. Native <option> and <optgroup> are rendered by the OS, which ignores custom properties. Two occurrences, same rationale.
The +2px in the collapsed icon width compensates for the border of the floating variant, so the rail lines up with the expanded sidebar.

w-[calc(var(--sidebar-width-icon)+var(--space-scale-4))] — the floating and inset variants sit inside a padded shell, so the collapsed rail measures its own width plus that padding. The sum is a property of the variant, not a value of the spacing scale.

left/right-[calc(var(--sidebar-width)*-1)] — the offcanvas panel is pushed out by exactly its own width, mirrored per side. The multiplication by -1 is the mirroring itself, and a token cannot carry a sign.

max-w-[calc(100%-var(--space-scale-8))] — the dialog is capped at the viewport minus one gutter on each side. The gutter is already a token; the subtraction from a width the component does not know cannot be one.

w-[calc(100%-var(--space-scale-8))] — the alert dialog is as wide as the viewport minus one gutter on each side, up to its max width. The gutter is a token; the subtraction from a width the component does not know cannot be one.

min-w-[calc(var(--anchor-width)+var(--space-scale-7))] — --anchor-width is measured by Base UI when the popup opens. The popup must clear the trigger plus room for the clear and chevron buttons; only that room is a token.

max-h-[min(calc(var(--space-scale-72)-var(--space-scale-9)),calc(var(--available-height)-var(--space-scale-9)))] — the list stops at the shorter of a fixed ceiling and the space Base UI measured below the trigger, both less the sticky input. The comparison is the behavior, not a size.

gap-[calc(var(--spacing)*var(--gap))] — shadcn/ui's `spacing` prop is a number of scale units, set as --gap on the root. The product of that runtime number and the scale unit cannot be a class of the locked spacing scale.

z-10 lays the stretched AttachmentTrigger over the media and the content so the whole attachment is one click target, and z-20 keeps AttachmentActions above it. Two occurrences, local ordering inside the attachment; the z-index scale addresses global layers (dropdown, modal, tooltip).
z-10 lifts BubbleReactions over the bubble they overlap, inside the bubble. Local ordering; the z-index scale addresses global layers (dropdown, modal, tooltip).

z-10 lays the transparent native input of a QuestionnaireChoice over its indicator and label, so the whole choice is the click target. Local ordering; the z-index scale addresses global layers (dropdown, modal, tooltip).

react-resizable-panels takes the minimum hit area of a handle as a number of px (resizeTargetMinimumSize) and measures it in JavaScript, where a CSS custom property does not apply. Its defaults (fine 10, coarse 20) are below WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8, so the group sets both to 24, the value of size.target.min.
